title: Prompt warmth and cache sim journal
content:
Purpose:
Quick informal lab notebook for thinking through what I keep calling 'prompt warmth' — how much a prompt + recent context warms local KV/prefix caches and how that affects latency/cost tradeoffs across different batching strategies. This is intentionally rough; will iterate.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Production: we see uneven token-costs and p95 latency spikes when many short conversational requests hit cold model KV caches.
- Hypothesis: small changes in prompt formatting (moving stable instructions earlier, bundling repetitive system tokens, explicit warmup tokens) can materially change cache hit-rate and per-token latency.
- Need a lightweight simulator to explore: request mixes, cache eviction policies, per-tenant affinity, and batching heuristics (time-window vs size-based).

High level goals:
- Build a micro-simulator to approximate token-level cache occupancy and hot-prefix reuse.
- Evaluate 3 axes: latency (p50/p95), per-token GPU compute cost, and model-state memory churn (KV reads/writes).
- Produce understandable knobs that could be suggested to customers or surfaced as Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Design sketch (simulator):
- Entities: Requests, Sessions (affinity groups), Model (seq-length, kv-size-per-token), Cache (LRU-like but TTL-aware), Batcher (window, size-limit).
- Request shape: {user_id, session_id, system_prompt, turn_id, tokens_out, tokens_in}. We'll represent as simple tuples in sim.
- Warmth metric: a per-request scalar in [0,1] representing fraction of prefix tokens that are already in cache. Compute estimated additional KV reads = tokens_used * (1 - warmth).

Simplified pseudocode for single step (rough):
- receive batch B of requests
- for r in B: compute r.warmth from recent cache snapshot (match longest prefix)
- cost_read += r.tokens_in * (1 - r.warmth) * model.kv_read_cost
- latency[token] = base_token_latency + extra_latency_per_kv_read * (1 - r.warmth)
- update cache with produced KV (e.g., append new prefixes up to K tokens)
- evict according to policy

Cache model details to try:
- Option A: pure LRU by prefix-hash granularity (prefix size = N tokens)
- Option B: hybrid TTL + freq score (decay and bump on access)
- Option C: session-local shadow cache (fast path) + global LRU (spillover)

Prompt warmup experiments (ideas):
- Baseline: current prod-ish mix from sample traces (need sanitized trace).
- Warmup variant A: duplicate first 5 tokens of system prompt in a compact warmup token chunk. Measure cache hit-rate change.
- Warmup variant B: move stable system tokens from head -> repeated small anchor at end of prompt (trade-off request-size vs reuse).
- Warmup variant C: canonicalize system prompts across tenants (lower entropy) to make them more cacheable.

Synthetic workload generator notes:
- Mix distributions: 70% short-chat (<= 64 in), 20% medium (64-256), 10% long (>256).
- Session stickiness: sample session lengths from geometric(p=0.1) — average ~10 turns.
- Tenant skew: Zipfian distribution for user ids so a few tenants create most traffic.

Metrics to capture per run:
- cache_hit_rate_by_prefix_length: 8 buckets (1-8,9-32,33-128,...).
- token_latency_histograms (p50,p90,p95,p99).
- per-token-gpu-cost and aggregate GPU-seconds.
- cold_start_fraction: fraction of requests that required > X KV reads.
- effective-throughput under batching policies: tokens/sec, requests/sec.

Quick ASCII diagram (flow):
Client -> Ingress -> Router -> Batcher -> Serving node -> Model kernel
                             |                          ^
                             v                          |
                         Cache lookup  <--------------- state updates

Open questions / things to watch:
- How to model token-level cache semantics without sim exploding in memory? Approach: coalesce identical prefixes and track counts rather than per-request entries.
- Warmth estimate: naive string match vs fuzzy-match (tokenized canonicalized sequences). Start naive.
- How to emulate KV backend latency curve? Use param: kv_latency = a + b * read_count^c (fit to observed infra).
- Session migration: what happens when a session moves between nodes (e.g., dedicated -> fallback)? Add occasional cross-node handoff events.

Experiment plan (first week):
1) Build minimal sim code in sim-tools repo (linked) that can ingest small synthetic workloads (seeded RNG).
2) Implement LRU prefix cache + windowed batching strategy. Produce baseline run.
3) Implement warmup variant A/B produce delta reports.
4) Create quick dashboard spreadsheet (CSV) with runs for review.

Notes for Redwood Optimize integration (brainstorm):
- Auto-suggest: "Consider canonicalizing system prompt (reduce unique head tokens)" — estimated savings: X% based on sim.
- Warmup token shim: small opt-in feature for Hosted API that allows a 3-token warmup blob with special flag to be cached strongly. Security review needed (prompt-injection risks?).
- Batcher hint: if sim shows time-window batching gives better p95 on small chats, surface as per-route config.

Safety / privacy considerations:
- Any canonicalization or warmup must be tenant-specific and not globally shared across tenants unless consented.
- Warmup tokens may contain PII — avoid storing raw warmup blobs outside ephemeral caches. Use hashed prefix keys with HMAC.

Action items / TODO:
- [ ] Get a sanitized 48-hour trace sample from observability team (obs-tickets JIRA-1127).
- [ ] Kickoff quick sim spike: assign to sim-tools PR (author: @noah-kim).
- [ ] Run baseline vs warmup A/B and collect metrics.
- [ ] Draft brief for Optimize team with suggested knobs and safety notes.

Rough timeline:
- Spike + baseline runs: 1 week
- Warmup variants & analysis: additional 1 week
- Internal review & notes: 3 days

Random heuristics / heuristics-to-test (brain dump):
- If session_turns > 6 then aggressively keep prefix cache entries pinned for that session.
- If tenant qps < threshold, avoid aggressive pinning (wastes global cache).
- Prefer canonicalized system prompts for tenants with > 10k monthly requests.

Slack references / links:
- #eng-runtime thread: slack thread id ~ C09F2345 (search: "warmth sim initial"), will paste results there.
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sim-tools/pull/87 (prototype code).

Closing thought:
I want this notebook to stay messy for now — it's where I capture intuition before formalizing into an RFC. If someone wants to run a focused sim, ping me and I'll carve out a reproducible config.
